newsitem.title: INDONESIA: BP sees increasing LNG competition in Asia.
newsitem.headline: BP sees increasing LNG competition in Asia.

text.p: Liquefied natural gas (LNG) producers faced increasing market competition to supply growing demand in Asia, British Petroleum Co Plc chief economist Peter Davies said on Wednesday.
"There is a whole range of supply options to supplying growing gas demand throughout Asia," he told a briefing in Jakarta on BP's statistical review of world energy for 1997.
Indonesia is the world's biggest LNG exporter and sixth biggest producer of natural gas.
Davies said Eastern Russia, Sakhalin and the Australian North Shelf, as well as the Middle East, all had the potential to produce LNG for the Asian market.
He said cutting production and delivery costs were the key to market share.

"It's going to be the ability to cut costs in all parts of the process and deliver the most competitive LNG on a contractual basis that is going to attract customers," he said, adding he anticipated growing competitiveness in the field.
Davies said he expected the linkage between oil and natural gas prices was breaking down, giving Britain as an example.
"We are getting gas-on-gas competition. I think the delinking of oil and gas prices is going to progressively happen, he said.
He said the delinking of oil and LNG prices would take a bit longer due to contractual obligations already in place.
Total Asia/Pacific natural gas consumption grew by 7.5 percent in 1996 over 1995 to 211 million tonnes of oil equivalent, according to BP statistics.
Indonesia has long-term contracts to supply LNG totalling more than 20 million tonnes a year to Japan, South Korea and Taiwan.
